title: Social Justice Studies: Asian American Studies

program.section_heading: Social Justice Studies: Asian American Studies - Associate of Arts for Transfer (ADT) - AA1072 (CalGETC)
outcomes: Understand the historical foundations of Asian American Studies and make connections with contemporary white supremacy and racial justice issues.
Read, write, and discuss orally a variety of texts written by and about Asian Americans and Asian American activism.
Use art, film, music, and literature to critically examine and explore the history and struggle of Asian Americans in the United States and throughout the Asian sub-continent.
Analyze the histories and experiences of Asian Americans and the contributions they have made to racial justice, social justice, and the fight for equality in the United States.
Examine the ethical and moral implications inherent in the experiences of Asian Americans in their quest for social, moral, and economic justice.
Compare and contrast Asian American experiences with other experiences that are a part of or separate from Asian traditions.
Use qualitative and quantitative research methods in the behavioral and social sciences to better analyze issues related to Asian American Studies.

notes: The catalog prints 'Units: 9.00' for the Required Courses section as a whole (ETS-1, the nested 'Select one of the following' choice of SOC-15/SOC-25, and ETS-40). Elective Courses: 'Choose three courses from at least two areas' (9.00-10.00). The areas are Area 1 History or Government (ETS-23/POLS-23, ETS-44/HIST-44, HIST-42), Area 2 Arts and Humanities (ARTH-12, ENGL-24, ETS-7, PHI-36), Area 3 Social Science (ETS-44/HIST-44, SOC-10/SOC-10H) and Area 4 Quantitative Reasoning and Research Methods (STAT-C1000/STAT-C1000H/PSYC-48/SOC-48). The at-least-two-areas constraint is not captured by the block structure.
ETS-44/HIST-44 is listed under both Area 1 and Area 3. It is recorded once in the elective block.
'Only one may be used' groups are recorded as one entry with alternatives: ETS-23/POLS-23, ETS-44/HIST-44, SOC-10/SOC-10H, and STAT-C1000/STAT-C1000H/PSYC-48/SOC-48.
